content.title: Arkansas vs. Arizona: Predictions, How to Watch for Free (3/26/26)
content.text: No. 4 Arkansas (28–8) faces No. 1 Arizona (31–4) tonight in the 2026 NCAA Tournament Sweet 16 at SAP Center in San Jose. Arkansas comes in off a 94–88 second-round win over No. 12 High Point on Saturday, with Darius Acuff Jr. taking over late to stave off the high-flying Panthers. Acuff led with 36 points on 11-of-22 shooting, also dishing six assists. With the game tied at 83, he scored seven straight points in the final three minutes to push the Razorbacks on top for good. Meleek Thomas added 19 points on 8-of-16 shooting. Billy Richmond III finished with a 15-point, 10-rebound double-double. Arizona comes in off a 78–66 win over Utah State on Sunday. Jaden Bradley led a balanced effort with 18 points, Brayden Burries followed with 16, and Koa Peat finished with a 14-point, 10-rebound double-double. The Wildcats’ only two losses came in mid-February, both by margins of four points or less. Prediction Both teams enter with tremendous offensive upsides, but Arizona has the edge here with its two-way balance. Expect the Wildcats to slow down the tempo late in the second half and secure a ticket to the Elite Eight. Predicted Final Score: Arizona 80, Arkansas 74 Tip-off for today’s game between Arkansas and Arizona is set for 9:45 PM Eastern / 6:45 PM Pacific. The game airs live on CBS. So you can tune in for free on your local CBS affiliate via antenna. CBS is also available at no additional cost through most cable, satellite, and live streaming packages. Today’s game also streams on the CBS and CBS Sports apps and websites, as well as Paramount+. If you’re a cord-cutter without an active livestreaming plan, you can watch the game for free with a Paramount+ 7-day trial, available through Amazon Prime Video here. You can also view the game for free by taking advantage of free trials from DIRECTV STREAM, Hulu + Live TV, Fubo TV, or YouTube TV.
